intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 15–19. No need to rush. You can look at the lessons again and try again as often as you want.
intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 15–19. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.

questions.0.question.note: Translator: 'Perspektif' is used for 'perspective'. Check that it matches the glossary word in Lesson 15. 'Sudut pandangan' is the other choice. 'Baju bola' is used for 'football shirt'. 'Jersi' is also common. Back-translation check: Translator flag still stands. Check that 'perspektif' is the glossary word in Lesson 15 ('sudut pandangan' is the other choice). Also check whether 'baju bola' or 'jersi' is better for 'football shirt'.
questions.0.question.back: A player sees a football shirt as part of the team. A fan sees it as a happy memory. They have different perspectives. What is the meaning of perspective?
questions.0.question.source: A player sees a football shirt as part of the team. A fan sees it as a happy memory. They have different perspectives. What does perspective mean?

questions.0.options.0.text.back: A person who makes something with their hands or tools
questions.0.options.0.text.source: A person who makes things with their hands or tools

questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. That is a maker. The player and the fan did not make the shirt. Look at Lesson 15 again.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. That is a maker. The player and the fan did not make the shirt. Look back at Lesson 15.

questions.0.options.1.text.back: The way a person sees or thinks about something
questions.0.options.1.text.source: The way one person sees or thinks about something

questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. A perspective is the way a person sees something. The player and the fan see the same shirt in different ways.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A perspective is the way one person sees something. The player and the fan see the same shirt in different ways.

questions.0.options.2.text.back: A picture or shape that represents an idea
questions.0.options.2.text.source: A picture or shape that stands for an idea

questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. That is a symbol. Here, each person sees the shirt in their own way. Look at Lesson 15 again.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. That is a symbol. Here, each person sees the shirt in their own way. Look back at Lesson 15.

questions.1.stimulus.title.note: Translator: 'Notes' means written comments, so I used 'catatan' and not 'nota'. Next to a drum, 'nota' could be read as musical notes. Back-translation check: 'Rekaan' (made-up) matches the key term 'Contoh rekaan', but the back-translator says it could be read as 'designed'. Check that 'Gendang rekaan' and 'Mural rekaan' clearly mean 'made-up' to young readers. 'Catatan' for 'notes' was chosen so it is not read as musical notes. Please confirm.

questions.1.stimulus.items.0.back: The seller said this drum is for playing music at events.
questions.1.stimulus.items.0.source: The seller says it is for playing music at events.

questions.1.stimulus.items.1.back: The owner said this drum reminds them of the day they joined the music club.
questions.1.stimulus.items.1.source: The owner says it reminds her of the day she joined a music club.

questions.1.stimulus.items.2.back: The maker said an older drum player taught them this pattern.
questions.1.stimulus.items.2.source: The maker says an older drummer taught her the pattern.

questions.1.question.back: A museum wants to make a label for this drum. Which label is best, based on Lesson 15?
questions.1.question.source: A museum wants a label for this drum. Which label is best, based on Lesson 15?

questions.1.options.0.text.back: This pattern is a symbol of the whole town and all its residents.
questions.1.options.0.text.source: The pattern is a symbol of the whole town and all its people.

questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. No note states the meaning of the pattern. A good label does not guess. Look at Lesson 15 again.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. No note says what the pattern means. A good label does not guess. Look back at Lesson 15.

questions.1.options.1.text.back: This is just an ordinary drum. It has no other meaning for anyone at all.
questions.1.options.1.text.source: It is just an everyday drum. It has no other meaning for anyone.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. The notes show that this drum also holds memories and skills. Look at Lesson 15 again.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The notes show that the drum also holds a memory and a skill. Look back at Lesson 15.

questions.1.options.2.text.back: For music. It holds memories for its owner and skill for its maker.
questions.1.options.2.text.source: For music. It holds a memory for its owner and a skill for its maker.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. This label uses what the seller, owner and maker said. It does not guess the meaning of the pattern.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. This label uses what the seller, the owner and the maker say. It does not guess what the pattern means.

questions.2.question.back: At Hillside Learning Centre, a volunteer talks about a food notice. Some visitors read the notice in English. Others use pictures, sign language or help from friends. What does this show?
questions.2.question.source: At Hillside Learning Centre, a volunteer talks about the food notice. Some visitors read the notice in English. Others use the pictures, sign language or help from a friend. What does this show?

questions.2.options.0.text.back: People can understand one message in different ways.
questions.2.options.0.text.source: People can understand one message in different ways.

questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The visitors use words, pictures, sign language or help from friends. They all get the same message in different ways.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Visitors use words, pictures, sign language or a friend's help. They all get the same message in different ways.

questions.2.options.1.text.back: Most visitors do not want to read the notice.
questions.2.options.1.text.source: Most visitors do not want to read the notice.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. The visitors really do want to know the message. They use different ways to understand it. Look at Lesson 16 again.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The visitors do want the message. They use different ways to understand it. Look back at Lesson 16.

questions.2.options.2.text.back: Only people who read English can come to the centre.
questions.2.options.2.text.source: Only people who read English can come to the centre.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. The notice states the food is for everyone. Many visitors understand it without reading English. Look at Lesson 16 again.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The notice says the food is for everyone. Many visitors understand it without reading English. Look back at Lesson 16.

questions.3.question.back: Lesson 16 states that no language is better than another language. What reason is given?
questions.3.question.source: Lesson 16 says that no language is better than another. What reason does it give?

questions.3.options.0.text.note: Back-translation check: Fixed: 'untuk sesuatu' read as 'for something'. Changed to 'untuk setiap benda' (for things). Check that it sounds natural.
questions.3.options.0.text.back: All languages use exactly the same words for something.
questions.3.options.0.text.source: All languages use the very same words for things.

questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. Each language has different words, and languages borrow words from each other. Look at Lesson 16 again.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Languages have different words, and they borrow words from each other. Look back at Lesson 16.

questions.3.options.1.text.back: Each language is spoken by the same number of people.
questions.3.options.1.text.source: Each language is spoken by the same number of people.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. This lesson does not count speakers. It discusses what each language holds. Look at Lesson 16 again.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson does not count speakers. It talks about what each language holds. Look back at Lesson 16.

questions.3.options.2.text.back: Each language holds the stories of its speakers.
questions.3.options.2.text.source: Each one holds the stories of its speakers.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. Each language holds the knowledge and stories of its speakers. So, no language is the best.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Every language holds the knowledge and stories of its speakers. So no language is the best.

questions.4.question.note: Back-translation check: 'Penganyam' (weaver) is correct but may be unfamiliar to young readers. Check that it is understood, or whether 'tukang anyam' reads more easily.
questions.4.question.back: In an invented village, older weavers show young people how to make baskets. Later, the young people will teach others. Which word from Lesson 17 names this?
questions.4.question.source: In a made-up village, older weavers show young people how to make baskets. Later, the young people will teach others. Which word from Lesson 17 names this?

questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. A celebration marks a special day with other people. Here, older people pass down skills to younger people. Look at Lesson 17 again.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A celebration marks a special day with others. Here, older people pass a skill to younger people. Look back at Lesson 17.

questions.4.options.1.text.note: Translator: 'Pewarisan' (the key term) usually means passing something down through generations. That fits here, but check that it also covers the feedback's definition: 'from one person to another'. Back-translation check: Translator flag still stands. 'Pewarisan' is the key term for 'transmission', but it can suggest inheriting property. Check that it fits the definition 'from one person to another' and that it matches Lesson 17.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. Inheritance means passing down knowledge or skills from one person to another. The weavers pass down their skills.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Transmission means passing knowledge or skills from one person to another. The weavers pass on their skill.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. A purpose is the reason something is done. Here, older people pass down skills to younger people. Look at Lesson 17 again.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A purpose is the reason why something is done. Here, older people pass a skill to younger people. Look back at Lesson 17.

questions.5.question.back: What does Lesson 17 say about traditions that change?
questions.5.question.source: What does Lesson 17 say about traditions that change?

questions.5.options.0.text.back: Traditions can change and still keep their purpose.
questions.5.options.0.text.source: A tradition can change and still keep its purpose.

questions.5.options.0.feedback.note: Back-translation check: Fixed: 'orang ramai' (the public) changed to 'orang', and 'ada hidangan baharu' changed to 'menambah hidangan baharu' (adds new dishes). Check that 'jamuan komuniti' matches the word used in Lesson 17.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. The community feast starts earlier and has new dishes. It still helps people meet, teach and welcome others.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The community meal starts earlier and adds new dishes. It still helps people meet, teach and welcome others.

questions.5.options.1.text.back: Traditions end as soon as people change them.
questions.5.options.1.text.source: A tradition ends as soon as people change it.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. People adapt traditions to new times, and the feast still goes on. Look at Lesson 17 again.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. People adapt traditions to fit new times, and the meal still goes on. Look back at Lesson 17.

questions.5.options.2.text.back: Only the oldest way is the right one.
questions.5.options.2.text.source: Only the very oldest way of doing it is the right way.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. Traditions do not stop in the past. People adapt them to new times. Look at Lesson 17 again.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Traditions are not frozen in the past. People adapt them to fit new times. Look back at Lesson 17.

questions.6.question.note: Back-translation check: 'Rock art' is translated as 'lukisan batu'. Check that it matches Lesson 18, or whether 'seni batu' or 'lukisan pada batu' is more natural.
questions.6.question.back: Lesson 18 gives three examples: rock paintings in Algeria, painted scrolls in China and sand drawings in Vanuatu. What do all three show?
questions.6.question.source: Lesson 18 gives three examples: rock art in Algeria, a painted scroll in China and sand drawings in Vanuatu. What do they all show?

questions.6.options.0.text.back: Art from long ago is always about animals.
questions.6.options.0.text.source: Art from long ago is always about animals.

questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. The rock paintings show animals, but the scroll shows a busy city full of people. Look at Lesson 18 again.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The rock art shows animals, but the scroll shows a busy city full of people. Look back at Lesson 18.

questions.6.options.1.text.back: People all over the world tell stories through art.
questions.6.options.1.text.source: People around the world tell stories with art.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. All three examples come from different places in the world. In every place, people use art to tell stories and keep knowledge.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The three examples come from different parts of the world. In each place, people use art to tell stories and keep knowledge.

questions.6.options.2.text.back: Only one place in the world tells stories through art.
questions.6.options.2.text.source: Only one part of the world tells stories with art.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. All three examples come from three different places. People all over the world tell stories through art. Look at Lesson 18 again.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The three examples come from three different places. People all over the world tell stories with art. Look back at Lesson 18.

questions.7.stimulus.body.back: A mural is a large painting on a wall. This mural is on the wall of an invented school. It shows a tall tree with long roots. Children of different heights hold hands around the tree. Above it is written “We grow up together”.
questions.7.stimulus.body.source: A mural is a big painting on a wall. This one is on the wall of a made-up school. It shows a tall tree with long roots. Children of different heights hold hands around the tree. At the top are the words “We grow together”.

questions.7.question.note: Translator: 'Interpretation' is translated as 'tafsiran'. Check that Lesson 18 uses the same word, so the question matches the lesson. Back-translation check: Translator flag still stands. Check that Lesson 18 also uses 'tafsiran' for 'interpretation'.
questions.7.question.back: Which sentence is an interpretation of the mural?
questions.7.question.source: Which sentence is an interpretation of the mural?

questions.7.options.0.text.back: This mural may be about teamwork.
questions.7.options.0.text.source: The mural may be about working as a team.

questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. This is an idea about the meaning of the mural. The joined hands and the words support it, and the word “may” shows you are being careful.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. This is an idea about what the mural means. The joined hands and the words support it, and “may” shows you are careful.

questions.7.options.1.text.back: Children hold hands around a tall tree.
questions.7.options.1.text.source: Children hold hands around a tall tree.

questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. This is an observation. Anyone can check it by looking at the mural. Look at Lesson 18 again.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can check it by looking at the mural. Look back at Lesson 18.

questions.7.options.2.text.back: Above it is written “We grow up together”.
questions.7.options.2.text.source: The words at the top say “We grow together”.

questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. This is an observation. Anyone can read the words on the wall. Look at Lesson 18 again.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can read the words on the wall. Look back at Lesson 18.

questions.8.question.back: An invented art club writes its meeting times in only one language. Some members cannot read that language, so they miss meetings. Which word from Lesson 19 names this problem?
questions.8.question.source: A made-up art club writes its meeting times in only one language. Some members cannot read that language, so they miss meetings. Which word from Lesson 19 names this problem?

questions.8.options.0.text.note: Back-translation check: 'Keupayaan bertindak' is the decided key term for 'agency', but it is long and abstract for a short answer option. Check that young readers recognise it as the Lesson 19 term.

questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. The ability to act is the power to make choices and act. This problem makes it hard for people to take part. Look at Lesson 19 again.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Agency is the power to make choices and act. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look back at Lesson 19.

questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. An opinion is what a person thinks about something. This problem makes it hard for people to take part. Look at Lesson 19 again.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. An opinion is what a person thinks about something. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look back at Lesson 19.

questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. An obstacle makes it hard for a person to take part. The club can share its times in more than one way.

questions.9.question.back: According to Lesson 19, what can a group do so that more people have a sense of belonging?
questions.9.question.source: What does Lesson 19 say a group can do so that more people feel they belong?

questions.9.options.0.text.back: Ask new members to share personal things
questions.9.options.0.text.source: Ask new members to share private things

questions.9.options.0.feedback.note: Translator: Here 'to belong' is 'berasa diterima' (to feel accepted), and results.high uses it too. The question itself uses the key term 'rasa kekitaan'. Check that both read naturally together. Back-translation check: Translator flag still stands. 'To belong' is 'berasa diterima' here and in results.high, but the question uses 'rasa kekitaan'. Check that both read naturally together.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. This lesson states that no one needs to share personal things to feel accepted. Look at Lesson 19 again.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says nobody should have to share private things to belong. Look back at Lesson 19.

questions.9.options.1.text.back: Change the way the group works
questions.9.options.1.text.source: Change the way the group works

questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The club does not need to change its members. It can change the way it works, for example with a taking-turns rule.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The club does not need to change its members. It can change how it works, for example with turn-taking rules.

questions.9.options.2.text.back: Ask members to behave like other people
questions.9.options.2.text.source: Ask members to act like everyone else

questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not accurate yet. This lesson states a group should change the way it works, not change its members. Look at Lesson 19 again.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says a group should change how it works, not change its members. Look back at Lesson 19.

results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about how people share meaning and help others feel accepted.
results.high.source: Well done. You know a lot about how people share meaning and help others belong.
